newsitem.title: USA: Group buying Frederick's of Hollywood for $53 million.
newsitem.headline: Group buying Frederick's of Hollywood for $53 million.

text.p: Frederick's of Hollywood Inc. said Sunday it agreed to be bought by an investment group in a $53 million deal that would take the lingerie retailer and catalog merchant private.

Knightsbridge Capital Corp., an investment bank based in Chicago, will lead a group of investors that will pay $6.14 a share for each of Frederick's Class A and Class B shares, Frederick's said in a statement.
Frederick's Class A stock closed at $5.25 and its Class B shares ended at $4.75 on the New York Stock Exchange on Friday.
Following the merger, Frederick's will be privately held and will continue to operate its retail and mail order businesses under its well known name.
The merger is subject to the approval of Frederick's stockholders and other conditions, and is expected to close by the end of July, the company said.
The company's board of directors has recommended that stockholders approve the deal, it added.

Frederick's, which lost $438,000 on sales of $148 million in the fiscal year ended on Aug. 31, 1996, is more than 50 percent owned by the family trusts of the company's late founder, Frederick Mellinger.
